quest.title: This Life, Just Like a Light Trickle of Song
quest.description: The members of the troupe do not see eye to eye on the ending of the script, and everyone believes they should hear what the last member, Vilmant, has to say on it. So, you set off from Poisson...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x675, Primogem x60, Mora x49200, Guide to Justice x5, Hero's Wit x6, Mystic Enhancement Ore x11

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Vilmant, are you there?

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: Huh? It's you guys... Wait, what's Lady Furina doing here!?

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: I can explain... We've been rounding up the whole troupe. We now have everyone except you.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Dulphy explains the whole sequence of events so far to Vilmant.

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: So, you think knowing the truth about the director's disappearance will help you write an ending to the script that pleases everyone?

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: *sigh* I care just as much as everyone else about making The Little Oceanid a success. That's why I wanted to wait until after the show.

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: If I open this can of worms now... I just don't want to make things difficult between us. We're supposed to be a unit when we're on stage.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Vilmant... Avoiding the truth will not help anyone.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Unless you mean to suggest that Aurelie's death had something to do with you?

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: I don't want to talk about it.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Listen, Vilmant. I used to think that my love for Aurelie was a point of shame. I never brought it up to anyone...

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: But now, I've made up my mind to put it all on the table. I'm prepared to face everything — to sacrifice everything — for the sake of the show.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: "The Little Oceanid" cannot be complete unless we do justice to Aurelie on an emotional level.

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: ...*sigh* This is why people think of you as not being the smart one.

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: As you all know already, the troupe was kept afloat not from ticket sales, but donations from the audience. Of course, that was nowhere near enough...

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: We took on side jobs when we weren't performing, but even then, the troupe's financial situation was pretty dire...

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: So anyway, one day after a show, a merchant came to me and offered us a huge sponsorship. In return, we just had to provide the audience with their drinks during performances.

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: It seemed like a win-win, so I said yes to it on the spot without consulting the director. It was only when the merchant came to deliver the goods that I realized...

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: The drink in question was... Sinthe.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...Isn't that the drink peddled by the culprit behind the serial disappearances case?

choices.text: I remember that it induces a state of euphoria.

response.speaker: Vilmant
response.text: I... I freaked out when I saw the boxes, and I told the director everything right away. She was completely shocked as well...

response.speaker: Vilmant
response.text: But she didn't reprimand me for making the decision without consulting her. Instead, she contacted the merchant, and stated that the troupe could not agree to this collaboration.

response.speaker: Vilmant
response.text: The merchant was furious, berated us for going back on our word, and threatened to sue us for damages. The amount was astronomical... There was no way we'd be able to pay...

response.speaker: Pauleau
response.text: A—And then...?

response.speaker: Vilmant
response.text: I was going to sort it on my own, but the director stopped me. She said that this was an issue for the whole troupe, and it wasn't my fault.

response.speaker: Vilmant
response.text: But things only got worse from there. The Sinthe merchant just wouldn't let up. Then, suddenly the director told us all to leave the city one day... I knew then that things must have reached a boiling point...

response.speaker: Vilmant
response.text: I admit it, this whole thing was my mistake. I didn't dare to tell any of you the truth back then, and after the director disappeared, I was even more afraid to say anything.

choices.text: You brought the director to the attention of the Sinthe dealers.

response.speaker: Vilmant
response.text: Yeah. I got Aurelie killed — there, I said it. Happy now?

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: Hey, don't say that...

response.speaker: Pauleau
response.text: You traitor!!! You knew Aurelie was in danger! Why in god's name didn't you tell us!?

response.speaker: Pauleau
response.text: What do you mean, you were "afraid"!? This was a life-and-death situation, we could have saved her!

response.speaker: Pauleau
response.text: How could you be so stupid!?

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Please, try not to get too worked up...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, listen to him! You need to stay calm!

response.speaker: Pauleau
response.text: Stay calm? How can I stay calm? This guy got Aurelie murdered! She was the love of my life!

response.speaker: Pauleau
response.text: And he has the gall to try and high-road us, claiming that he kept his mouth shut for the sake of the show! How about taking some responsibility for what he's done?

response.speaker: Vilmant
response.text: All I can say is I'm sorry. Truly. I wanted to apologize... to everyone in the troupe. But that won't bring back the director. What good is my apology now?

response.speaker: Vilmant
response.text: I'm just a coward who made an awful, terrible mistake that I can never take back. Beat me up if you want — kill me if you prefer. It's what I deserve.

response.speaker: Vilmant
response.text: End my life! So I can meet the director and apologize to her in person!

response.speaker: Pauleau
response.text: Get out of my sight! Go, get lost! I don't ever want to see your face again!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: That's enough! You've screamed and shouted at each other for long enough. Now pipe down, both of you!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Can you stop conflating the show on stage with your real-life relationships in the troupe?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: You keep saying that you want to use this final performance to pay tribute to your director and celebrate her life. How can you do that if you're just using it as an excuse to vent your own emotions?

response.speaker: Pauleau
response.text: ...You're right.

response.speaker: Vilmant
response.text: I'm sorry.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: On stage, the lead role is the focal point of the audience's attention, and you're all used to seeing the director as the heart of the troupe.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: But in her own life, her greatest desire wasn't to be the center of attention... I can tell how much she loved you all, and how much she loved the troupe.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: What she wanted was to build a warm home for all of her brothers and sisters. To shield you all from the storms that rage in the world outside. That's how you should remember her, and that's what you should be celebrating.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I understand why you're trying to make her the hero of the story, but... isn't she your hero already? After everything she did for you?

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Yeah.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: So think hard about what that means. And then think again about what you hope to achieve by arguing with each other.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: If you really hate each other, and can't reconcile your differences, then you could just call it quits now. Why bother with a final performance if the group is already fractured?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: But you can't bring yourself to do that, can you? You care too much about Director Aurelie and the home she built you all to let go.

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: Hehe.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: What are you laughing at? I don't see what's so funny.

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: Sorry, I didn't mean it that way. It's just that... for a moment there, I... It felt like our director was back with us again.

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: If she'd seen Pauleau and Vilmant at each other's throats like that, she would have scolded them exactly like you did, in that same stern voice.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? But she sounded like such a gentle person...

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: Of course she was. Even her harshest lectures came from a place of kindness, and it showed. She really was a truly outstanding person.

response.speaker: Pauleau
response.text: I... What you said, it... really puts everything into perspective.

response.speaker: Vilmant
response.text: I'm truly sorry. I really meant for this to be a genuine apology, but... I ended up making it all about me and my self-pity.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: It's alright. Let's save all this for after the performance.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sooo... The ending. What are we gonna do about it?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Clearly, everyone needs to take a step back for now, and reflect on what really matters. When emotions are running high, things get lost in the fray.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: The end of the story needs to focus back on Aurelie herself. She's the true star of the show.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: It might actually be possible to find out more about her fate.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What do you mean?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: The Traveler is right. You once investigated that underwater Sinthe base, and recovered items belonging to the victims.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: If you could find anything that Aurelie left behind... Perhaps we can get a better sense of what she went through in her final days.

response.speaker: Pauleau
response.text: You really think that's possible?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I trust that nobody would object to the ending of the story being based on Aurelie's true feelings?

response.speaker: Vilmant
response.text: No...

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Well, we'll leave this in your capable hands.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Come, let's pay a visit to the Palais Mermonia. The rest of you, head back to the rehearsal location for now, and wait for our good news.

choices.text: Your mistake gave them a motive to kidnap and murder her.
But it also causes significant harm to the body.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh, as if this journey wasn't tough enough already without a roadblock!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: #Don't worry, we should all be fine with {NICKNAME} here. We don't need to take a detour.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...Wait, wh—why are you all looking at me? You're not seriously expecting me to fight, are you!?

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: We're just curious, that's all. I don't think anyone's ever seen Furina in a fight before...

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Yeah, but... Don't you remember why? The Hydro Archon willingly gave up all of her power so it could be converted into Indemnitium. Miss Furina said so herself.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Precisely! Heh... And I'm not even the Hydro Archon anymore, so all my power is gone anyway.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: As much as it pains me, unfortunately, I should just stay put. I'm more like... a damsel in distress more than anything.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That sounded so smug! Ugh, the second-hand embarrassment is unbearable...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: C'est la vie indeed! Alas, I am forced to watch on helplessly as a more brave and seasoned adventurer than I swoops in to save the day.

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: Ah, too bad... I was so pumped to feast my eyes on fight-mode Furina.

response.speaker: Lauwick
response.text: Sorry to leave all the heavy lifting to you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Don't worry — piece of cake!

choices.text: This doesn't require god-level powers. Don't you know any self-defense?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Hey, lay off, alright! My bluff is hanging from a thread here.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I'm sorry, I'm sorry... I got carried away. Please help us out, would you?

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: ...You want to review some recovered items connected to victims of the serial disappearances case? But... that case has been closed for quite a while now.

dialogues.speaker: Sedene
dialogues.text: Still, since you were the ones who discovered and submitted the evidence in the first place, you don't actually have to submit an application... Okay. Please hold on — I'll have someone dig them out.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Sedene sends a staff member to retrieve the box of Aurelie's former belongings.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So this is all Aurelie left behind... Just whatever she was carrying on her person, and this tattered old notebook.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, it's full of script lines... and sketches, too. Looks like they show where the different props should be placed on-stage.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Let me take a look. Maybe there's something in here from after she was kidnapped...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Aha! I found something. "To whoever discovers this diary"... Let's see...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Looks like she kept a detailed record of her captor's actions. She even mentions the truth behind the "experiments" on dissolving young women.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: If we'd had the chance to examine this notebook carefully back then, it would have been a conclusive piece of evidence, proving Vacher's guilt.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Vacher took so many lives... It's still so unthinkable, how many victims he had.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I guess Aurelie must have written all of this down in the hope that her records would one day be of use to investigators.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Wait... it cuts off...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Uh, is something wrong?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Her handwriting here gets patchier and more illegible by the line... She probably didn't have much strength left.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Her final words are... I'll let you read them for yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: She was so terrified...

choices.text: She watched a girl get dissolved right in front of her...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: She may have been a mighty hero in the eyes of her troupe, but... at the end of the day, she was only human.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I can't bear to think how painful and lonely her final days must have been...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Wait, this part on the last page sounds strangely familiar...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: "If you become human... You can reveal your secret to no one. You will face suffering and loneliness. Is this truly what you want?"

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Isn't that the most important line in "The Little Oceanid"?

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: "Because I am an older sister to them."

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Ohhhhhh...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: So she didn't regret her decision. Even as she sat in silence, waiting for death to come.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I'm sure this is what the troupe would have hoped to hear as well.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: She had their utmost trust, admiration, and love... And she truly deserved it.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Let's go. It's time for them to learn Director Aurelie's final thoughts.

choices.text: And had to wait for her own death in silence...

talks.objective: Continue onward to where Vilmant is
Look for the former troupe director's belongings in the Palais Mermonia

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: After reading through the notebook, some are lost for words, some weep bitterly, and some grind their teeth and howl with rage...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A long time passes before the group is able to calmly come together and finally make a decision.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: She deserves a hero's farewell. If that's the only way to convey to the audience the courage and selflessness that she showed in the face of death, then it's a meaningful way to end the story.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Even in the last moments of her life, she was still leaving a trail for others to follow.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: She did her best to protect as many people as possible, even if it meant sacrificing herself...

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: We know what choice our "Little Oceanid" would have made now. I don't think any more discussion is necessary.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Well, Vilmant? If we put the past aside for now, do you think you can bring yourself to go ahead with the show?

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: ...I will channel all my regret and put it into my performance, to make this a show worthy of our director.

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: I won't ask for your forgiveness, and you don't need to worry about my feelings. This final farewell show should be about director Aurelie, and her alone.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Then it seems like we've reached a consensus. I have a feeling that this will turn out to be the most mesmerizing performance of your lives.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Really? How can you be so sure when you've never even seen them perform before?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hehe, don't underestimate my experience. After watching a countless number of musicals, I've learned one important thing.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: If you want to move the audience with your music, you must fully commit and immerse yourself in your role, pouring all your emotion into your performance.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: And aren't human emotions — love, hate, regret, and hope — just the most mesmerizing things in this world?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I don't believe anybody could be more committed to bringing this story to life on the stage than they are now.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Thank you for the vote of confidence, Miss Furina. And thank you for supporting us through all this.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Then let's not delay things any longer. We need to discuss the details of the ending, and get it nailed down once and for all.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Actually, before that, I'd like to make a proposal.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: During the curtain call, please allow me to use the director's name instead of my own.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Eh? But then...

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: After all, this role was originally meant to be played by the director. I'm just filling in for her.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Besides, a role commemorating her life should be associated with her name.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Well... If you're sure you're okay with that, I have no objection to it.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hehe, now we're talking like a serious acting troupe!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Alright, I'll leave you to fine-tune your musical while I go and procure a stage.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Procure a stage?

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Oh, it's okay. Our usual place doesn't need a reservation...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: That place? Don't be silly! For an extraordinary show, we need an extraordinary stage... By which I of course mean, the Opera Epiclese.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Whoa, wait... what?

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: No, no, no... That's never going to work. It's far too fancy for the likes of us...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: What are you afraid of? Surely you don't think that Aurelie's story is unworthy of the grandest stage in Fontaine?

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: Uh... No, that's not what I meant...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It is supposed to be your grand finale, right?

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: I have no problem with it then, how about the rest of you?

response.speaker: Dulphy
response.text: ...I'll take your silence as a yes! Haha. Thank you for giving us this opportunity... It really is a dream come true.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Well, then don't disappoint me!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: If you mess this up, it'll reflect poorly on me, too!

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Come on. We'll need to get the go-ahead from Neuvillette — I know just where to find him.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I knew you'd be here.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I am here merely for a short break. It has been a while, Miss Furina. And you too, Traveler and Paimon. What might I assist you with today?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I would like to book the Opera Epiclese for an event. You see...

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You share the story of "The Little Oceanid" with Neuvillette, along with the backstory.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I understand. Hmm, the process for booking the Opera Epiclese is complex and can be somewhat cumbersome... But given that the request is coming from the three of you, I see no reason to make things unduly difficult.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The story of the "The Little Oceanid" is most fascinating. I am looking forward to seeing it performed onstage.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I will say, however, that I am surprised to see your passion for the performing arts rekindled after all that has happened.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean? ...Do I look excited?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Yes. And this is the first time that I've seen you like this since your departure from deityhood.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: At first, I just felt bad about rejecting them, so I wanted to learn a little bit more about their situation. But one thing led to another, and... Well, here we are.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: In the past, we sat in our high chairs in the court, giving our opinions on isolated cases, all while knowing very little about the human stories behind each and every one.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Maybe it's because I've finally become an ordinary person, and gained my freedom, that I've developed a great sense of curiosity about their lives.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I am truly delighted to see you find a new lease on life.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Now that you've regained some confidence, have you had any thoughts regarding a return to the stage?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...Why would you suddenly ask a question like that?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Well, if "The Little Oceanid" turns out to be a great success, it will no doubt become a classic. Many theatre companies are certain to add it to their repertoire.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: The experiences and decisions of the protagonist, Clio, are all modeled after your own. Naturally, this makes you eminently suited to playing the leading role.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: It would truly be a shame if you did not take this opportunity to allow audiences to enjoy your outstanding acting talents once more.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Haven't I already made myself clear? I won't act or perform in any role ever again. No exceptions.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Nor do I think it is any great shame. There is no lack of fine actors or inspirational stories, either on or off the stage.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: This experience is a case in point. I feel like I've learned a lot, and it has already been well worth the price of admission.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I must admit, though, I'm a little envious... They're quite fortunate to be able to bid farewell to their past in such a magnificent manner.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I see. Well, I'm glad to learn that you have found a role to play that you enjoy, be it on the stage or not.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I sincerely hope the show will serve as the grandest of finales. I will have my staff book the date, and mail the relevant paperwork to the troupe once the details are confirmed.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks, Neuvillette!

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: You're very welcome.

talks.objective: Return to the rehearsal location and assist with the rehearsal

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Good news, everyone — it's done! The Opera Epiclese is booked.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Thanks to my eloquent and impassioned speech, Monsieur Neuvillette was moved to provide us with a fitting stage for this special performance.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: We've had to fight every step of the way for this opportunity, but we now have all of the ingredients necessary to stage a truly spectacular performance:

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: A touching story, a magnificent venue, and last but not least, a passionate and dedicated cast!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Now, let's work together, and make this show the best it can be!

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Hehe, this is truly wonderful.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: The sooner we can finalize the ending, the more time we'll have to rehearse.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Vilmant and I just went over some parts of the script and tweaked a few things. I think it's really going to resonate with the audience now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, you two had a constructive conversation? That's great!

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: Communication is vital to any good performance.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Haha... Look at us! We've come so far. I never could've pictured this scene a few days ago...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's amazing... Even though Furina's still being a bit of a drama queen about it all, she's really fired everyone up!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I'm really looking forward to the final production.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Please feel free to give us any comments or suggestions you have. We really value your input.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Hey, Lauwick, get over here. Time to practice the opening number.

talks.objective: Go to the opera house to assist with the performance

dialogues.speaker: Ciamaca
dialogues.text: That cursed Clio, she stole the waters of life from us! She's a fraud, and she must pay for her crimes!

dialogues.speaker: Perroux
dialogues.text: This has nothing to do with her! The ignorance and hatred of our people is to blame. How can we hope to win back the water's favor if we don't change our ways?

dialogues.speaker: Ciamaca
dialogues.text: This guy could be useful... Take him hostage! If Clio wants him back, she'll have to show herself...

dialogues.speaker: Perroux
dialogues.text: Leave this place, O Little Oceanid, and never, ever look back!

dialogues.speaker: Audience
dialogues.text: *clap*

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Everyone's really throwing themselves into their roles. I haven't seen such a fine performance in a long time.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: *sigh* If only...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What should we do? It's almost time for her to take the stage...

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Ugh... Why, why does it have to be now...

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Hey, what's going on? You're due on stage any second now...

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Oh no, not again... But why? What about your new meds? Did they stop working?

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: They've... been getting less and less effective over time. I've had to keep increasing my dose...

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: What!? I thought they cure it... So they were only managing your symptoms?

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: I figured... whatever it took to get me through this final performance...

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: How could you do this to yourself? And after that lecture you gave me about not looking after my health!

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: ...I'm sorry. I've let everyone down.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: You... *sigh* This is a conversation for another time. How can the show go on without its star performer?

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Miss Furina... I'd like to make a request of you.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Say no more. If you're sick, you need to rest. I know what you're going to ask.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Lauwick, your character has no more scenes, correct?

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Oh, uh... Yeah, I think my scenes are all done. Although... I do have one more line, but I guess another guy in the troupe with a similar voice register could take it. Why?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Please take Dulphy back to her place to rest. I'll sing the finale.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...*sigh* From the sublime to the ridiculous... After all that, everything's come full circle.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Thank you, Miss Furina... I'm so sorry to put you in this position after everything you said...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Never mind, what's done is done. It's really my own fault for getting in too deep, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: No one likes regrets, myself included.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Leave it to me. I've watched you rehearse so many times that I've learned Clio's part by heart.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: I do not doubt your acting skills, but please allow me to ask just one more question. After all, this show is dedicated to the life and legacy of our director...

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: What, in your opinion, is the reason Clio shines so brightly?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: ...It's her pure heart.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Despite all the pain and loneliness she had to endure... She never once stopped believing in the beauty in this world.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: ...Well said.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: I leave Director Aurelie in your hands.

dialogues.speaker: Veillas
dialogues.text: Is it just me, or... was that Lady Furina on the stage just now?

dialogues.speaker: Gignac
dialogues.text: She hasn't been seen for a while now, and she just appears out of nowhere...

dialogues.speaker: Gignac
dialogues.text: Gotta say, though, her acting skills are as superb as ever!

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: The Little Oceanid, Clio. Played by Aurelie Fumeau.

dialogues.speaker: Veillas
dialogues.text: Wait, that's not her name. What's going on?

dialogues.speaker: Gignac
dialogues.text: I dunno. Maybe it's just a doppelganger?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (I've spent a lot of time out of the spotlight, and they didn't use my name during the curtain call either. Hopefully, not too many people recognized me...)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (It's too bad that I had to break the one clear rule I'd managed to make for myself... Even if I had no choice...)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (Still, I have to admit that, despite everything...)

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: (...It felt good to be back on the stage again.)

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Finally, we would like to give a special thanks to our artistic consultant and event coordinator, Miss Furina!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hey! That's not what we agreed on!

dialogues.speaker: Veillas
dialogues.text: Ooooh, so it was Furina after all!

dialogues.speaker: Gignac
dialogues.text: She's back!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Aaaah! Ugh, honestly, what is he doing! He should have run that by me first...

talks.objective: Talk to Furina and the troupe members

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Alright, calm down, don't be mad. This was a group decision. We just didn't want your contributions to go unacknowledged.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: After all, it's been the rule in Fontaine since ancient times that everyone's work, visible or invisible, is equally deserving of recognition.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Yes, I know the rule, but... but... Ugh, it should still be applied on a case-by-case basis! I wasn't ready for this yet!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, it's no big deal. What's the worst that could happen?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: At most, you might be asked to sign a few autographs later.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh yeah? Well, since you think it's so easy, you can sign them for me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is a great chat and all, but can we talk about that crazy thing that happened during the show? It nearly gave Paimon a heart attack!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon flew over to where she was supposed to be, and was about to drop the prop Vision, and then suddenly... a real one popped out of thin air!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Oh, that...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I've got no idea what happened there, either. But hey, it worked pretty well, didn't it?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I'll bet the audience has never seen such a realistic prop.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Wait, what about Dulphy? I wonder how she's doing.

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: Let's go check on her as soon as we finish clearing the stage.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Yes. Plus, she'll definitely want to hear how the end of the show went...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: If nothing else, we can safely say that we accomplished what we set out to do.

talks.objective: Return to see Dulphy and Lauwick

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Ah, you're back.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: She's doing okay. Her condition stabilized after taking some of her original medication. From experience, though, I'd say she still needs a few more days of rest.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: How did the performance go? Was it a success? Did the audience like it?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You'll be glad to know it was fantastic! Also, you're not gonna believe what happened while Furina was on the stage... You'll probably be able to read all about it in the Steambird first thing tomorrow morning.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: That's wonderful...

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: I'm so sorry I failed to see it through to the end. I guess I was wrong to try and tough it out to begin with.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Don't worry about it. Like they told me after announcing my name during the curtain call — everyone's work deserves recognition.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Even though you couldn't see it through to the final scene, the audience was very impressed by your performance. It's safe to say that you made your mark on this memorial show.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Mm. Well, one way or another, we did it.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: I've had bad luck ever since I was born, so I never expect things to go smoothly in life... I'm just happy to know that we went out on a high note. That's all that matters.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Blaming your bad luck again, are we? Maybe if you didn't push yourself past your limits so much, your illness wouldn't be flaring up all the time.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Oh, don't you start... I don't have the energy to argue with you right now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Aww, you two clearly care a lot about each other.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Hmph, I don't know what you're talking about.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: You mean, we never stop arguing with each other.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: So. Any plans for the next step?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: After the brilliant performance you put on, the reputation of your troupe is sure to spread through Fontaine like wildfire. You won't have to disband if you don't want to.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: You could capitalize on the rave reviews and license out "The Little Oceanid" to the bigger theater troupes out there. That would do wonders for your financial situation.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: No, we should still disband.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Yeah. It's what we all agreed to.

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: After all that's happened, I should give you guys some space. But maybe our paths will cross again one day.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, don't just walk off! Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: I still want to keep performing, so I might join another troupe.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: After watching Miss Furina's performance, I think I'm starting to understand our director's infatuation with musicals.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Hehe, you should do it. It suits you. I'd originally hoped to keep performing too, but... I don't know if my health will allow me to.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Oh, so now you've finally got your priorities in order... *sigh* I guess I'll hold off until you've properly recovered as well.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: What about you, Miss Furina? Any future plans?

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Well, frankly, I think a return to obscurity is no longer an option for me. I'm sure a slew of consultancy requests will hound me wherever I go, until I finally acquiesce.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: You rather sealed my fate there, with your "special thanks" at the end of the show.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: Sorry...

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: It's quite alright. No need to apologize. What I meant to say is that... This whole experience has shown me that perhaps I'm not as averse to a return to the stage as I'd previously imagined.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Maybe Neuvillette was right... Maybe "Clio" is the right role for me.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: I still don't wish to pretend to be someone else, but I do have a desire to express myself... So maybe the show will go on for me after all.

choices.text: There's no need to draw lines in the sand.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Yeah. There was once a time when I was an actress in a masquerade, seeking only to hide the truth...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: But from now on, I want to spend my time learning real stories about real people, and how they touch the lives of others around them.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I want to watch them blossom and wither, see them refined on the page, retold on the stage, and remembered long into the future.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: I'm sure this is what captivated Director Aurelie as well.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Sounds like you're ready to stop running from your true calling.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: The more you get out into the world, the more you'll discover what a fascinating place it is.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Next time, I'll invite you to join me.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Hehe, then it's a deal.

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: If a Vision is a gift from the gods...

response.speaker: Furina
response.text: Then I should do my best to honor it.

choices.text: Just do whatever feels right to you.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: First Miss Furina, now the Opera Epiclese... If only the director was still with us.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Hey, come on. There's no point in dwelling on that now. We have a lot of work to do.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Yeah, you're right. Now's not the time to get all melancholy.

dialogues.speaker: Vilmant
dialogues.text: ...Best of luck to you.

dialogues.speaker: Pauleau
dialogues.text: During the final scene... Maybe we should stop the music just before Clio takes the stage?

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: Many people were once enthralled by Lady Furina's performances, myself included.

dialogues.speaker: Neuvillette
dialogues.text: I hope that one day, she'll be able to understand that our appreciation was always sincere.

dialogues.speaker: Veillas
dialogues.text: What a surprise, seeing Miss Furina on the stage... This ticket was money well spent.

dialogues.speaker: Gignac
dialogues.text: Yeah, I agree... Say what you want about her, but she's flawless when she's on stage.

dialogues.speaker: Sabine
dialogues.text: I thought Clio's actress sang very well... Why did they swap her out at the end?

dialogues.speaker: Tussaud
dialogues.text: I dunno. Maybe that's just how it was scripted?

dialogues.speaker: Kirimoto
dialogues.text: Did anyone see where Miss Furina went? I want to get her autograph, but I can't find her anywhere...

dialogues.speaker: Connie
dialogues.text: I wasn't expecting such an incredible performance from an amateur troupe. They didn't seem out of place on the big stage at all.

dialogues.speaker: Evra
dialogues.text: Yeah. Their technique could use some polish, but the performance in general felt very believable. Hit all the right emotional notes. I think it'll stay with me for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Lauwick
dialogues.text: Whew, this is tough going... Dulphy, are you sure you can manage in your condition?

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Hmph, I could ask you the same question! Try to keep up.

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Bravo, good show! You certainly live up to your reputation.

dialogues.speaker: Dulphy
dialogues.text: Yeah, thank you... Anyway, the path is cleared now. So, onwards and upwards!

dialogues.speaker: Furina
dialogues.text: Hey, look at that! Looks like I guessed right.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You were just guessing!?
